notes.title: Rival Restaurants: Ignite Your Culinary Ambition!
notes.content:
[img]https://f.tabletopia.com/n/013/248/s1141pagtvadcbtzjyxlj3.png[/img]
[h3][b]Welcome to [url=https://tabletopia.com/games/rival-restaurants]Rival Restaurants[/url]![/b][/h3]
 
Where the sizzling excitement of culinary competition meets the thrill of high-stakes strategy!
 
This isn’t just a board game; it’s your chance to step into the spotlight and transform your culinary dreams into a reality. In this electrifying showdown, you’ll manage a bustling restaurant, face off against rival chefs, and navigate a dynamic culinary landscape.
 
Are you ready to rise to the challenge and turn your restaurant into the city's most coveted dining destination?

[img]https://f.tabletopia.com/n/013/248/pvtvupcei0p8awyegwwli0.png[/img]
[b][h3]Objective: Claim the Title of "The Wiener"[/h3][/b]
In Rival Restaurants, your ultimate goal is to be the first to earn 20 popularity points and be crowned “The Wiener!” Achieve this by acquiring and trading ingredients to complete mouthwatering recipes. The more complex and sophisticated the recipe, the more points it’s worth. 
 
[b]Your journey unfolds across three action-packed phases each day:[/b]
 
MONEY & MOVE: Start each day by collecting your income and strategically choosing your location. Once you’ve made your choice, you’re set for the day, so select wisely. This phase sets the stage for your day’s decisions, so plan your moves with precision.
 
BUY & BARTER: With a minute on the clock, buy as many ingredients as you can from your current location and trade with other players. This phase is where your negotiation skills shine – secure the best deals and build a stockpile of essential ingredients to create winning recipes.
 
COOK & COUNTER: If you’ve gathered all the ingredients needed for your recipe, it’s time to cook and earn those valuable popularity points. After cooking, restock the counters and prepare for the next round of culinary action.

[img]https://f.tabletopia.com/n/013/248/wzrqgeanyd855fe30z3avd.png[/img]
[h3][b]Unleash Your Chef’s Unique Power[/b][/h3]

Every player commands a unique chef, each equipped with their own special powers.
 
These asymmetrical abilities allow you to bend the rules and gain a competitive edge.
 
With twelve distinct chefs to choose from, you’ll find strategies and tactics that fit your playstyle. At the start of the game, select from a variety of restaurants, each offering a unique progression path with special rewards for reaching popularity milestones of 3, 7, and 12 points.
 
Enhance your strategy further by acquiring action cards – powerful, one-time-use cards that can turn the tide of the game.

[img]https://f.tabletopia.com/n/013/248/efddxemo8qfugbhwinxc82.png[/img]
[b][h3]Why Rival Restaurants Will Keep You Coming Back for More:[/h3][/b]
Thrilling Real-Time Competition: Experience the excitement of fast-paced gameplay where every decision matters. The game unfolds over three dynamic phases each day, providing constant opportunities and challenges. Each playthrough is unique, ensuring that you’re always engaged and ready for the next round.
 

Diverse Restaurant Themes: Dive into a rich variety of restaurant themes, each offering distinct strategic advantages and gameplay elements. Whether you’re running a high-end fine-dining venue or a bustling street food market, each theme presents its own set of rewards and challenges. Choose wisely and tailor your strategy to fit your theme, ensuring that no two games are ever the same.
 

Engaging Head-to-Head Battles: Immerse yourself in the heart of culinary competition. Use powerful action cards and create inventive recipes to outmaneuver your rivals. Every card and recipe plays a crucial role in your strategy, making each decision and action critical to your success.
 

Strategic Depth: Winning in Rival Restaurants requires more than just culinary skills. It demands astute strategic thinking and effective management. Balance your budget, optimize your menu, and navigate the competitive landscape to build a restaurant that stands out from the rest.
 

Unforgettable Culinary Experience: Rival Restaurants offers an immersive culinary adventure filled with memorable moments and intense competition. Experience the thrill of managing your own restaurant, competing with other chefs, and serving dishes that captivate and delight your customers. Every game session promises strategic depth and excitement.
 

Dynamic Challenges: Face a series of dynamic challenges as you progress through the game. Unexpected events, evolving customer demands, and rival strategies will test your skills and adaptability. Each challenge adds complexity to the game, making your quest for culinary supremacy even more engaging and rewarding.

[img]https://f.tabletopia.com/n/013/248/gqmyv5h4bdibrpkfjo3zs2.png[/img]
[b][h3]Endless Variety for Unmatched Replayability[/h3][/b]
Rival Restaurants offers unparalleled replayability with up to 12 unique chefs, 8 diverse restaurant themes, and 48 different recipes.
 
No two games are ever alike, ensuring that you’ll always have a fresh and exciting experience. The innovative “all together” mechanism keeps everyone engaged, eliminating wait times and enhancing the game’s strategic depth. Easy to learn but challenging to master, Rival Restaurants caters to both seasoned gamers and newcomers alike.
 
Get ready for non-stop fun as your friends will undoubtedly want to play again and again.

[img]https://f.tabletopia.com/n/013/248/jzbes6gtngdz09ajncztdc.png[/img]
[h3][b]Meet the Chefs Who Make Rival Restaurants Sizzle![/b][/h3]
 
In Rival Restaurants, chefs have a variety of unique abilities that add strategic depth to the game.
 
These abilities can include ejecting other players from their location, increasing the cost of purchases for others, substituting one ingredient for another with bonuses, replacing meat ingredients with vegetables, and forcing other chefs to switch locations for a fee. Other abilities might involve blocking counters for other players, transferring garbage items to others, receiving free ingredients with purchases, buying action cards without visiting special locations, and making other chefs pay money at the end of a phase.
 
Each ability impacts the game, creating unique tactical opportunities and diverse gameplay scenarios.

[img]https://f.tabletopia.com/n/013/248/dzzvz1v5udctwv7gzyn2rn1.png[/img]
[h3][b]Discover the Exciting Kitchen Squad Mode[/b][/h3]
 
Elevate your gameplay with the exhilarating Kitchen Squad Mode in Rival Restaurants!
 
This innovative 2-player variant introduces a new level of strategy and excitement. In this mode, you will oversee the operations of three chefs while working alongside an NPC (non-player chef) who acts as a semi-ally. The addition of the NPC not only adds a new layer of strategic depth but also provides opportunities to disrupt your opponent's plans and access additional markets.
 
This dynamic gameplay ensures that every decision you make is crucial and impactful, transforming each game session into a thrilling culinary showdown.
 
[b]Committed to Perfection[/b]
 
At Rival Restaurants, our commitment to delivering an exceptional gaming experience is unwavering.
 
We have meticulously crafted every aspect of the game to meet the highest standards of quality and detail. Our dedication is reflected in the thoughtful design and production processes that ensure Rival Restaurants not only meets but exceeds your expectations. With our game, you can anticipate a flawless experience that will quickly become a favorite feature of your game nights. We take immense pride in our work and are confident that Rival Restaurants will provide endless enjoyment and become a cherished addition to your collection.

[previewyoutube=0yZDhBtaX2Q;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3][b]Embrace the Challenge and Claim Your Culinary Fame![/b][/h3]

Step into the culinary spotlight, embrace the challenge, and showcase your creativity. Serve up a winning combination of flavor and strategy as you compete to become the ultimate restaurateur.
 
The kitchen is your stage – rise to the occasion and let your restaurant shine as you claim your place among the culinary elite!
 
Join the culinary showdown and make your mark in Rival Restaurants today!

[url=https://tabletopia.com/games/rival-restaurants][b][h3]Play it now on Tabletopia[/h3][/b][/url]

notes.title: The third and final expansion to Tapestry!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/ad481e60d05a04cd7c696b41c28045ec63f35002.jpg[/img]

Parallel universes are abundant in the world of [i]Tapestry[/i]. The [i][b]Fantasies & Futures expansion[/b][/i] gives players the opportunity to build civilizations using fantasy and sci-fi inspired civs, technology, tapestries, and cities.

[previewyoutube=J5FzMpkbasM;full][/previewyoutube]
In this third and final expansion to [i][url=https://tabletopia.com/games/tapestry]Tapestry[/url][/i], 10 new civilizations, 6 advanced capital city mats, 38 new tapestry cards, and 12 new tech cards are accompanied by a comprehensive rulebook that organizes all rules for Tapestry and the 3 expansions in one place (as well as a few replacement cards from previous expansions: 3 landmark cards, Oil Paint, and Migration).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/b7b468bf74b25f7a95c25a69b199af2b44c54b34.jpg[/img]

Some of the new tapestry cards include a new “charm” mechanism that provides one-time bonuses; some new tapestry and tech cards include exciting payoffs reserved for the final income turn.

[i]Fantasies & Futures[/i] is fully compatible with any combination of the core game, the other [i]Tapestry[/i] expansions, and the natural rubber playmat. It is packaged in an eco-friendly, recyclable envelope.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/08fb597b68afb7b49fdfcb79b84e47c6be57bc11.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Win the favor of the Gods in this epic auction, area-control game
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/bf836abda33bfcb41aa992ca5d254d00223d74db.jpg[/img]

In the Cyclades archipelago, off the shores of a divided Greece, players develop their cities and compete for supremacy under the watchful gaze of the gods.

[previewyoutube=Ur-ZmUgfNxE;full][/previewyoutube]
In [i][b]Cyclades: Legendary Edition[/b][/i], designers Bruno Cathala and Ludovic Maublanc have reworked the Cyclades base game and its many expansions to make gameplay more dynamic and fluid.

[previewyoutube=nCRkwW66Jlw;full][/previewyoutube]
The game features a strategic bidding system that defines the actions available to each player on their turn. You must balance your finances to optimize the various actions provided by the different gods, with each player gaining the support of only one god each turn. The game features a shorter and more dynamic bidding phase than the original Cyclades thanks to a new exponential bidding scale. Six gods are available instead of the five, increasing the variety of actions available:
[list]
[*] Ares allows the movement of player armies and the building of fortresses.
[*] Poseidon allows players to move their navies and build ports.
[*] Zeus allows his followers to hire priests and build temples.
[*] Athena provides her worshipers with philosophers and universities.
[*] Apollo increases the income of his worshipers.
[*] Hera provides mercenaries to enforce your troops during battle.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/ec5b1b2017b7a676456b3208c00a7753fdf52ff4.jpg[/img]

Players now use landscape tiles to assemble the modular game board during set-up, allowing for ever-changing maps and game strategies. New creatures and heroes are available in the base game, offering new strategic opportunities to build metropolises and gain decisive advantages on the battlefield. Your goal is to be the first to control three metropolises, which can be obtained as follows:
[list]
[*] Economic development, by constructing four different buildings.
[*] Intellectual development, by owning four philosophers.

notes.title: What classics do you want to play on Tabletopia?
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/3a50203631458594c418d8ad77a05d2c81a20b22.jpg[/img]

Are you a fan of classic board games, but find it difficult to get your hands on them? Have you ever wanted to see rare and out-of-print games from gaming history, but can't visit a physical museum? Then Tabletopia has some exciting news for you!

We're thrilled to announce our upcoming project, the Board Game Museum. This digital museum will showcase the biggest and greatest retro games and out-of-print classics in gaming history, all in one convenient location. These classic games will be available for a new digital audience through our best-in-class Unity 3D, in-the-browser application.

We want to make sure the Board Game Museum features the games that you, the players, want to see. That's why we're asking for your input! We've created a short survey with just four questions to help us determine what you'd like to see in this project!

So whether you're a die-hard board game enthusiast or just curious about gaming history, we want to hear from you! Take the survey and share it with your friends and fellow gamers to help us create the ultimate digital archive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/128472b510ae254bbae41e94ca9085eba4c8f4fc.jpg[/img][i]We want to hear what you want to see![/i]

To give you an idea of the games our users have suggested, we received a wide range of responses to our end-of-year survey. Some of the most popular classic games mentioned include [i]Grand Austria Hotel, Warhammer Quest: The Adventure Card Game, Glory to Rome, Stone Garden, Hive, Monopoly, Guild Ball[/i], and [i]Magic Realm[/i]. We also received requests for older and harder-to-find games such as [i]Dozo, Snapshot[/i], and [i]Stellar Conquest[/i].

Thank you for your participation, and we can't wait to share the Board Game Museum with you soon! Stay tuned for updates on our release date and more information about the exciting games that will be featured in the museum.

notes.title: 3 expansions for the dice-rolling worker placement game
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/57e04b43c59779d1bb2ef00c31326d6b373dbd0e.jpg[/img]

[i][b]Dice Hospital: Community Care[/b][/i] is the new box with 3 expansions for the original game: [i]Dice Hospital[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/575e11773113a7bc6623a5d36b3d19f1145de441.jpg[/img]

[h3]"The City" Expansion[/h3]

The intake phase is now replaced by a set of city tiles where players use their ambulances and paramedic tokens to collect patients.
This vastly increases interactivity, as now players have a direct say over which specific dice you pick up, as well as bonuses gained by picking up unhealthy patients! But watch out, any patients left in the city who have not been tended to, neglect in value and the player(s) who picked up the healthiest patients that round gain fatality tokens, if the worst happens to the patients! This expansion also includes a helicopter miniature (used to pickup patients from anywhere in the city grid for whoever is the first player that round) in the Kickstarter edition.

[previewyoutube=ifVPwO6Rk1M;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]"The Maternity" Expansion[/h3]

This expansion includes normal sized pink mother dice and smaller pink baby dice! This expansion also increases interaction by making players compete for objective cards set by the "city" to ensure a good amount of mother and baby dice are discharged (with often other colour combinations) by the end of the game. This also includes a new spatial element to the game in which mothers only neglect when untreated and in a ward with other dice. Players also roll the birthing die to see whether they receive single or twin babies!

[previewyoutube=Yb70GDvOtMc;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]"The Improvements" expansion[/h3]

This expansion allows for almost unlimited customisation! Players will be given a free-to-visit worker placement board where they can pick up room improvements specific to a colour of their choice. This expansion vastly increases the crunchiness of the game and is for players who have played the original game "wanting more".

notes.title: Tabletopia 2.0 coming soon!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/fd51b132f8e2c62b95e45748798060a7d391e2e1.png[/img]

We are happy to announce that this year Tabletopia engine will get the most fundamental update in its history that will radically improve its performance, graphics, and usability for both players and game designers. There's so much new stuff that we call this update Tabletopia 2.0.

Since its creation in 2015, Tabletopia has been a unique innovative tool that lets you play and experience virtual 3D board games from your web browser. However, technology progresses and now in 2022, we are able to make things even more beautiful and convenient for our users.

[url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/tabletopia/tabletopia-the-digital-platform-for-board-games][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/9b30481f76b7d3f0d7e883c2400e5290d0f0254c.png[/img][/url][i]Kickstarter felt like a lifetime ago![/i]

Here are some of the changes to come:

[h2]GRAPHICS AND PERFORMANCE[/h2]

First, graphic performance will be much better without increasing loading time and required memory space. At the moment, even though playing in a web browser gives you 100% of the Tabletopia experience, we recommend playing in the Steam app because graphics quality, resolution, and overall performance are clearly better. In Tabletopia 2.0 you will not see this difference anymore because the browser experience will be the same as in the application.

[h2]GAMEPLAY ENHANCEMENTS[/h2]

Second, many new features will be added to make gameplay smoother. We regularly receive requests from you for features like an “undo” button (letting you cancel the previous action), the ability to search through decks and bags, the ability to type and draw on the game components, tools to measure distances, customizable hotkeys etc. All this and much more will be implemented in the new engine - watch this space to keep informed about new features!

[h2]FLESHED OUT CREATION TOOLS[/h2]

Last but not least, the game creation process will go through the most drastic changes. It will take place completely in the game client, i.e. on the table. You will be able to upload any objects directly to your table, customize it, multiply, scale, or group. This will make game design and prototyping much easier and open new possibilities for your creativity. But what is most important, this new feature set will help not only game designers but also the players - you will be able to customize your game in action by changing or uploading any objects. Don’t want to play with standard meeples again? Upload your models or make simple standees from photos of yourself and your friends!

We plan to launch the new functionality for game design this fall and will keep you updated about new features and other improvements!

notes.title: "Ready To Play" & "Ready To Teach" Now Available
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/1e75397e5d202e0ba5694508b4cfc8bbb7c3c63b.png[/img]

To make finding the right person easier, you can now add games to “ready to teach” or “ready to play” lists near the Experience section of your [url=https://tabletopia.com/profile]Profile[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/3edb54ec127eb975bb17ac2bf6ad72a66239da08.png[/img]

If you mark a game as “Ready to TEACH” it means that you know the game quite well, enjoy it and are ready to share your knowledge and experience with others teaching them how to play. Only users with the rank “Expert” or “Veteran” in a particular game can choose this option.

If you mark a game as “Ready to PLAY” it means that you like the game and will be likely to accept invitations to play but are not ready to explain all the rules - just looking for co-players. In both cases, your preference will be seen in the leaderboard of the game so people looking for experienced players will be likely to contact you when looking to playing the game.

You can also quickly mark these options on the individual pages of each game by clicking their respective boxes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/f335874a8a1f437ceae6915dbc1f5d93d097432a.png[/img]

And finally, if you want to try a game, but don’t know the rules or want to just look for someone to play with, open its leaderboard and find those who have already confirmed that they are ready to teach and/or play. Just send them a [url=https://help.tabletopia.com/knowledge-base/chat-messaging/]message[/url] and introduce yourself!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/297269b194c27fc6cc15713d15a51e8b01c92e0f.png[/img]

We hope that these tools – combined with our [url=https://help.tabletopia.com/knowledge-base/player-experience/]Player Experience[/url] & [url=https://help.tabletopia.com/knowledge-base/chat-messaging/]Chat[/url] tools  – can encourage you to try something new, or help you find new players for a game you already love!

[h3][b][url=https://help.tabletopia.com/knowledge-base/how-to-learn-and-teach-games/]You can review this information at any time from our Knowledge Base.[/url][/b][/h3]

notes.title: Add allies and mid-turn tactics to your Zorro adventure!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/2566e45912639938a4ef4b994dd6a621ffea5184.jpg[/img]

An aging and battle-weary Zorro can no longer adequately defend the people from oppression so he must now find a worthy successor. Prove yourself to him by showing your heroism and proficiency in battle by defeating the scoundrels and villains that are persecuting your fellow citizens. After the final battle, it will be clear who deserves to wear the mantle and become the next Zorro! Will it be you?

[previewyoutube=2vV5nhHCk9Y;full][/previewyoutube]
Gather equipment in [i][b]The Zorro Dice Game[/b][/i] by defeating heroic feats in Yahtzee/King of Tokyo-style dice rolling, either alone or with another player helping. Collect sets of heroic feats to earn more dice that only you can use, but that will also trigger a scoundrel or a villain. Once the villain emerges, whoever defeats them will win the game and become the next Zorro!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/322ddf1b2d3bade7bc86fbc1a94806474851d2ea.jpg[/img]

The [i][b]Stunts & Allies[/b][/i] expansion to [i]The Zorro Dice Game[/i] gives each player an Ally, who will level up throughout the game, providing your hero with special abilities and a subtle catch-up mechanic. If your Ally reaches its max level, you will unlock your own, personal Ally Die as well. But each Ally has a weakness that you have to mitigate as you fight Scoundrels and Villains, which increases the difficulty of the game overall.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/e7a6b27219b3b42fdae4c189b2f2834efd9de590.jpg[/img]

Stunt Tokens were added as well, which offer additional opportunities for mid-turn tactics, like switching Heroic Feats or re-rolling dice.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/b6e3d37d4ef08e8c8795e5bdf5a745bee3b00dae.jpg[/img]

Lastly, it will add more Equipment, Scoundrels, and Villains to the base game as well for additional replayability and more combos to try in your overall strategy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/0d1175f8710920c0e1c3cd3aa5e9f84e9cf957e0.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Compete to see the most rare birds as you travel through western North America
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/1b9af836b63b2a2a3d59c32c77515f949a94d5f0.png[/img]

Grab your binoculars and your birding journal because it's time to hit the trails and see some birds. Choose a habitat each round to visit along the western coast of North America, and see what rare birds you can find. Don't forget to keep an eye on what your fellow birders are tracking down — they might just lead you to the bird that finishes your watch list and earns you extra points! Who will outsmart their opponents, spot the most birds, and be the best birder?

[previewyoutube=8VxhQY2jaEM;full][/previewyoutube]
In [i][b]Birds of a Feather: Western North America[/b][/i], you and the other players explore different habitats to spot birds. In the first round, each player chooses and reveals a card from hand, then marks off on their score sheet or the app the bird they played as well as all other birds played in the same habitat. The deck contains cards from five habitats, with some birds being more common than others. In the second round, you each play a card again, then you mark all birds in your current habitat as well as all cards played the previous round in that habitat. Apparently word spread about all the great finds! Remove all cards from the first round, then keep playing additional rounds in the same manner.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/ed6f63d24fc11e8b14a2471271272a142a9c342a.jpg[/img]

When each player has only one card left in hand, the game ends. For each ace bird you've seen in a habitat, you score 2 points; for each other non-common bird you've seen, score 1 point; and if you've seen all seven types of birds in a habitat, score 3 bonus points for a total of 10 points in that habitat. Whoever has the most total points wins.

[i]Birds of a Feather: Western North America[/i] reimpliments [i]Birds of Feather[/i] with new graphic design and improved rules for two- and three-player games to make them more strategic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/1c0c8dbd7df7bd883e888943e4838eb7f80d16b2.jpg[/img]

[previewyoutube=HlI3vOoZHmM;full][/previewyoutube]
In [i][b]Orléans[/b][/i], you will recruit followers and put them to work to make use of their abilities. Farmers and Boatmen supply you with money and goods; Knights expand your scope of action and secure your mercantile expeditions; Craftsmen build trading stations and tools to facilitate work; Scholars make progress in science; Traders open up new locations for you to use your followers; and last but not least, it cannot hurt to get active in monasteries since with Monks on your side you are much less likely to fall prey to fate.

You will always want to take more actions than possible, and there are many paths to victory. The challenge is to combine all elements as best as possible with regard to your strategy.

notes.title: More ways to create the most beautiful garden
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/1737e5d3e493072d7f536ed325f70f96d07550b3.jpg[/img]

Welcome to a delightful realm of beautiful gardens, vibrant flowers, and eye-catching scenery. Take up your spade and hone your finest gardening skills by crafting and nurturing the most majestic display of natural beauty, much to the envy of your neighbors over the wall. Lounge beneath your freshly-watered trellis and sip a cup of tea with fresh mint. Enjoy an afternoon in the sparkling world of [i][b]Flourish[/b][/i], a place you will want to return to time and time again.

[previewyoutube=t9t8bPWCTuM;full][/previewyoutube]
[i][b]Flourish[/b][/i] is a beautiful, card-drafting, garden-building game in which players plan and build the garden of their dreams over the course of the growing season. With delightful imagery, players plan their gardens throughout the game to collect the most points.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/ec7f7cddd1a342678e6f77074e947076ae22af00.jpg[/img]

This easy-to-learn game offers both competitive strategy and co-operative game modes, and a 1-7 player count provides a high level of accessibility and replayability.

The Tabletopia version of [i]Flourish[/i] has been updated to include the [i][b]Friends & Follies expansions[/b][/i]. Play with either or both expansions at the same time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/e71fb355413cd8d273b38533b55294a6092be882.jpg[/img]

Many creatures, such as bees, bats, and even some snakes, can be very beneficial to a garden. Avid gardeners will often try to make a welcoming atmosphere for these animal friends. In the [i][b]Friends expansion[/b][/i], craft your garden to make a welcoming environment for friendly critters!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/0a4099afa723cf6efdba8a22b67545b66aab9935.jpg[/img]

A folly is a building or some kind of structure designed primarily for decoration, and usually serves no other purpose than providing visual interest or whimsy to the surrounding landscape. In the [i][b]Follies expansion[/b][/i], build magnificent structures that compliment your garden in beautiful ways!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/644e21ce4665c25dfba1064e219ce93a071f46af.jpg[/img]

notes.title: The ultimate SimCity-like city building game
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/2ff7481c041eef2bc1fb58ee8fcb5c76b4879202.jpg[/img]

You are the mayor of one borough of [i][b]Small City[/b][/i], and you have eight turns to secure enough votes to be re-elected. To do this, you have to attract more citizens, encourage the growth of residential areas for them to live in, and aid the expansion of both the commercial and industrial sectors – though the latter sector also brings pollution with it, and you need to deal with that, too, as high pollution levels will have a negative effect on your score at the end of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/8f35c06904308af76c0fd12be3cfea9815d63e01.jpg[/img]

If you build suitable infrastructure, your citizens will undoubtedly vote for your re-election, but beware of false promises! Votes can be earned over the course of the game by placing citizens in the residential spaces, by erecting cultural buildings, by keeping commercial buildings in suitable areas, and also by making good on the promises that you made to the citizens at the beginning of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/9767649ca6cfd3d2f309291d0e9e6eefcfb99e07.jpg[/img]

The player with the most votes (i.e., victory points) after eight turns wins.

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/f2ed820cfcbb1fd1d41646725005514cb81feb12.png[/img]

[i][b]Aye, Dark Overlord![/b][/i] is a fantasy party game filled with humor that's fast to play and easy to learn.

[previewyoutube=GXSkF-vLHUs;full][/previewyoutube]
Each player is an evil goblin servant of the evil Dark Overlord — Rigor Mortis, the Master of all Evils — and all of them are gathered at the Dark Overlord's knees to explain why they brought that last important mission, ordered by "His Evil Excellence" himself, to failure again. Panic wraps you in its freezing grip; what can you do to save your poor skin? Could you say you are not the one to blame, but your inept companions? Yes, of course, that's the solution! notes.title: The classic 1986 game about the world's most lethal car race - RELOADED
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/b0657db95f7d25a6b1159d572d24d5968944c04c.png[/img]

[i][b]Thunder Road: Vendetta[/b][/i] is a revved-up restoration of the classic 1986 game of mayhem on the asphalt. Grab your crew, roll your dice, race your cars, shoot your guns, and try not to get wrecked. This is a game of fast turns, high interaction, and dicey decisions. When all else fails, CALL IN THE CHOPPER!

[previewyoutube=x5TZE8NzcmQ;full][/previewyoutube]
Rocket your team (three cars and a helicopter) down a stretch of post-apocalyptic highway and try to either wipe out the other teams or outdistance them and leave them in the dust. Each turn consists of a dice roll to determine car movement and a combat phase where you try to shoot or ram your opponents. The gameboard consists of two pieces of highway and when the lead car exits the front piece of highway, the back piece is placed in front (after dumping all the wrecks and slowpokes off of it) thus creating a never-ending gameboard.

[previewyoutube=Lrq-lo1BdAY;full][/previewyoutube]
This new version features exciting new additions, including random hazard tokens, such as wrecks, oil slicks, and more. Damage isn't merely one and done. Now, you'll draw damage tokens with exciting effects that can send your car careening across the board. You'll also have more choices on your turn, assigning one of your dice to your command board to repair damage, nitro boost, or send out your attack copter to fire away.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/8f618e870c65d733ab0075434997e339e5f4431e.png[/img]

notes.title: Deal with unruly peasants and maintain your beautiful summer palace
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/f58421b48ea7dff6dc0724caeb66805400a3bb25.jpg[/img]

In [i]Gùgōng[/i], players take on the role of powerful Chinese families trying to gain influence and power by exchanging gifts with Officials. The gift cards you offer as a player have to be of a higher value than the one you receive, forcing you to make strategic choices regarding which actions you want to take each turn. You will travel around China, sail down the Grand Canal, purchase precious jade, help construct the Great Wall, secure advantages through decrees, influence the game through intrigue, and ultimately, receive an audience with the emperor.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/2d7c424b3da2f6d884a707e613ef190d848cba14.jpg[/img]

[i][b]Gùgōng: Pànjūn[/b][/i] is an expansion for the critically acclaimed Gùgōng. The 4 different modules can be combined however players wish to, guaranteeing a lot of variety and replayability. The 4 modules are:

[list]
[*] [b]The Summer Palace[/b]: Players travel to the Summer Palace of the Emperor, where they can obtain extra servants, Jade, and even the services of the mysterious Court Ladies… Players will have to score majorities in order to obtain these bonuses, but will also be able to manipulate the results by exchanging specific Gifts with the officials, as word has it the Emperor is collecting a very particular type of Gift.
[*] [b]The Peasants Revolt[/b]: During the Ming Dynasty, peasants revolts were common. Although the Ming Dynasty itself came to power through a peasant revolt, this did not mean that the rulers had any more empathy for the peasants than the previous rulers. Players will gain a lot of support from the peasants in this expansion, but if pushed too far, players will have to work together to avoid their wrath.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/20e84aaaa38f8254d98b0b82ce0973e767134a2e.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]The Palace Stairs[/b]: Moving your Envoy towards the Emperor will not be without consequences with this expansion module. Players will be able to choose a longer or shorter path leading towards the Palace of Heavenly Purity. The shorter path will require some achievements, the long path will earn players rewards at first, but when they get close to the Palace, they will have to pay certain taxes or risk seeing their Envoy take steps back.
[*] [b]Extra Decrees and Gift Cards[/b]: Spice up your game with new Decrees and special kinds of Gift Cards, like the lamp and jade knives, which will add even more variety to your game of Gùgōng!
[/list]

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/7fd78a77c2676ba4e73fe7e55d6c46321cfaceb6.jpg[/img]

As a Free Captain of the Rim you roam the far reaches of space as a trader and mercenary. Secretly though you are an agent of the Intergalactic Council sent on a clandestine mission to explore planets infiltrated by three alien races known as The Cosmic Hegemony who plan to invade the peaceful worlds of Intergalactic Alliance.

notes.title: Will you make a fortune mining tin and copper in 19th Century Cornwall?
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/f29ce53053438e48738f98e9df6c42e4d54f3d08.jpg[/img]

In [i][b]Tinners' Trail[/b][/i], set in 19th century Cornwall, you represent a mining conglomerate at the height of the tin and copper mining industry. You must buy plots of land across Cornwall in auctions and survey them for tin and copper, always managing your "work points" and money effectively.

[previewyoutube=CeBiMSGoClg;full][/previewyoutube]
Once you have a mine in place, it's time to extract the ore and (ideally) make a profit, but the deeper your mine goes, the more expensive the process gets. To reduce the cost of mining, you can place developments, such as ports, train stations, and adits (drainage tunnels), but there's only so many improvements to go around. Once you have made your money — trying to time the market to sell when prices are high — you can invest it in industries outside of Cornwall, which gains you victory points. The earlier you invest, the better the return. Can you outplay the competition and make the most money, or will you be left without two shillings to rub together?

[previewyoutube=4MRMhT841CE;full][/previewyoutube]
This edition of [i]Tinners' Trail[/i] differs from the original 2008 version in several ways. The player count, for example, is now 1-5 instead of 3-4, and the resources on the board are now set up via tiles instead of die rolls to maintain variability while reducing the randomness. Dual-use cards are now an important part of the game, giving you information before an auction or an extra boost after an auction.

notes.title: Chat & Player Experience Added Sitewide
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/f61897a7ae4b42cdc7ccef0f07ab715212178f67.jpg[/img]

We're excited to announce that 2 new features have rolled out on Tabletopia for all players! With the addition of site-wide chat & player experience/leaderboards, we want to help encourage players to connect and learn something they maybe haven't tried before.

[h1]Player Experience & Leaderboards[/h1]

You can now see every game you've ever played on Tabletopia in the “Experience” row in your profile. Simply go to your Profile while browsing Tabletopia and scroll down to the "Experience" row. In the upper left corner, you can see your total playtime and rank in every game.

Rankings are assigned by:
[list]
[*] "Beginner" = Less than 2 plays
[*] "Expert" = Between 2-5 plays
[*] "Veteran" = More than 5 plays.
[/list]
[i]Note: A “play” is based on the average playtime for the particular game. For example, if the average game of [b][url=https://tabletopia.com/games/calico]Calico[/url][/b] takes 38 minutes, you will need to have logged 76 minutes of playtime to have “2 plays” (regardless of how many game rooms/sessions you have joined). Tabletopia detects when you are inactive from a game, so leaving your screen open and walking away won’t help you boost your playtime![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/7a7952ed02237cdbfe4e47c160203db8c0200423.png[/img]

On every game page you can see the Leaderboard in the left column: these are the most experienced players ranked by playtime. You can switch to the “Month” tab to see only those who played the game in the last thirty days. If any of your friends have played the game, you will see a “Friends” tab to view their playtime.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/b5261a1016a3664c14d29ced10cb902005353523.png[/img]

If you click “More” below the leaderboard, you will go to the full leaderboard page for that game.

If you do not wish to be seen in leaderboards, go to your Profile -> Manage Account -> untick “Display my profile on Leaderboards”.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/780a3d12cfffd13f0d08052e6986c216ed9da371.png[/img]

[h1]Chat & Messaging[/h1]

You can now start a private chat with any other player on the site. This is designed to work in tandem with the Player Experience features and allow people to approach experienced players for a teaching game (or a duel!).

[b][h3]Abuse of the messaging system will not be tolerated, and Tabletopia reserves the right to suspend any account harassing other users.[/h3][/b]

You will see a chat icon on the bottom right of your screen while browsing the site, and you can use this to search for users via username and manage multiple chats. When you have a new message, you'll see a bubble notification to indicate unread messages.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/ce7dde9583ada6557270b408e19c696d1cbf73bc.png[/img]

You can quickly send your friends a message by going to the "Players" tab, howevering over their profile, and clicking the "send message" icon.

If you hover the mouse over any player in the Leaderboard, you will see an icon to send them a message (for example, to suggest playing the game) and a star icon to add them to your friends list. Also, you can see which languages the person speaks if they provided this information in their profile.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/62f3a151f0dc37a55f1deacc4a4be1225ea02d10.png[/img]

Happy gaming!

[i][b]Maharaja[/b][/i] is a new edition of the classic game by the authors Wolfgang Kramer and Michael Kiesling. In this new version of the game which now supports 1 to 4 players and is enriched with new graphics and components, you build statues of your God of reference to please the Maharaja during their visit and score victory points at the end of the game depending on the majority you reach.

[previewyoutube=tAYQUn6unqA;full][/previewyoutube]
During the game, players take the role of priests who travel to different cities in India, building statues and shrines dedicated to their favorite Gods to expand their worship. To do so, they are assisted by several characters with different abilities. At the beginning of each year, players plan their actions in a secret phase to be played simultaneously.

At the end of the seventh year or when a player builds their seventh statue, the game ends, then the player with most prestige wins.

notes.title: Alexander's generals fight amongst themselves to succeed his empire.
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/7f7bf44697018ff59ccd56fbcb8ea324cc369726.jpg[/img]

[i]When Alexander the Great died in 323 BC, he left no clear heir to the immense empire he had conquered. It was not long after his death that the Macedonian generals began to war among themselves over who would be the regent or successor to Alexander's empire. By 305 BC they had given up on succession and began to carve out their own kingdoms.[/i]

[previewyoutube=Zk_5ig2GK_k;full][/previewyoutube]
[i][b]Successors[/b][/i] is a 2-5 player card-driven wargame based on those wars.

[previewyoutube=t9Xema_vEVY;full][/previewyoutube]
Lose yourself in one of the best multiplayer strategy games ever published. Take part in the conflict between titular diadochi – [i]Successors[/i] – to the legacy and empire of Alexander the Great. Clash with your former brothers in arms turned enemies to gain control of provinces in order to increase the number of your Victory Points or pull appropriate strings to secure the Legitimacy Points e.g. by providing Alexander’s tomb with a suitable resting place. But beware, too many Victory Points with respect to other players and you end up having the esteem of a Usurper who could be attacked freely by everyone.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/cfec94a860afe25a212216abb95b594a77793217.jpg[/img]

Therefore, choose your strategy wisely. It sometimes is more profitable to hold your horses for every aspect of the game is intertwined with another and the sudden turn of events may surprise you with the most unfortunate outcome, for instance, you might be forced to take sides with someone who stabbed you in the back couple of rounds earlier. However, as they must have said even in 4th Century B.C., the end justifies the means. Especially, when succession is at stake.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/f5171405df42f751ed3b520c5db78710f86b1b38.jpg[/img]

[i]Successors[/i] was first published in 1997 by Avalon Hill. Some years later a second edition rulebook was published that gave more options for the Tyche cards. Then [i]Successors[/i] III, built on the foundation of the [i]Successors[/i] II rules set plus expansion cards, appeared in the Boardgamer.

The fourth edition of [i]Successors[/i] includes more generals, more scenarios, new Tyche cards, plenty of new components, and a changed map, with Libya and Cyrene being merged.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/bef57b021b2f068ca07bf82e4027a7585a3e4bff.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/eda9f8afd9f39c8697a682d9abdf97f574da5377.jpg[/img]

[i][b]Clash of Deck[/b][/i] is a two-player, expendable game with many twist, the biggest of which is: you buy a folded, 8-pages booklet and cut the cards off to build your game.

[previewyoutube=vs9SJTC7xko;full][/previewyoutube]
Released on a monthly basis, the game sees the player summon creature on each side of two bridges on two different lanes and attack their opponent to try and destroy first their watchtower, and then their castle. To do so they first must dispatch opposing creatures.

[previewyoutube=ruppJmm6q7A;full][/previewyoutube]
When a player suffers damage, they move their watchtower/castle card from left to right in their hand. If the building reaches the rightmost position, it is destroyed.

[previewyoutube=wnmaF7bx3bo;full][/previewyoutube]
Since the number of cards in one's hand is the amount of mana the player gets at the beginning of their turn, and defeated creatures go back into your hand on the rightmost position, knowing which creature to play and which creature to let die is key to managing both your position on the board and your life total.

Haven Town is facing total annihilation at the hands (and teeth) of a horde of monsters from beyond the Shadowrift.

[previewyoutube=Twg1iPDbloo;full][/previewyoutube]
You, the heroes, must band together to drive them back. To do this, you will need powerful spells, skills, attacks and loot. When the game begins, you are a basic hero; you can explore and fight. Luckily for you, [i][b]Shadowrift[/b][/i] is a deck-building game! You can buy new cards to add to your deck, cards that will define you as an adventurer and complement the strengths of your fellow heroes. Unlike other deck-builders, there is constant interaction with your fellow players as you figure out who will gain which benefit from the limited supply of townsfolk, offer their coin to help construct walls, and seek healing from anyone who's learned such magic.

[previewyoutube=4w48YKrEsWI;full][/previewyoutube]
[i]Shadowrift[/i] also features monsters that don't merely sit waiting to be slain; if you leave them alone, they will rip Haven Town asunder. They'll kill people, break walls, and kick your heroes in the face. Combat with them is intuitive (though frequently painful). For defeating a monster, heroes gain Heroism, a simple, consistent boost to their power that makes them better at anything they undertake. Since the monsters won't stop coming until the last Shadowrift is sealed or the town has been built into a mighty fortress, you'll need every boost you can take.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/fe5842845b759de915588ff7aae0b9b6ff769d18.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Step further into Simon Stålenhag's stunning retro scifi world
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/fb2d089fdc012d392fcf83ac892332b5b8a04799.jpg[/img]

[i]The landscape was full of machines and scrap metal connected to the facility in one way or another. Always present on the horizon were the colossal cooling towers of the Bona Reactor, with their green obstruction lights.[/i]

[previewyoutube=23NXBPARVQ0;full][/previewyoutube]
[i]If you put your ear to the ground, you could hear the heartbeat of the Loop – the purring of the Gravitron, the central piece of engineering magic that was the focus of the Loop’s experiments.[/i]

[previewyoutube=eXGxHZFlscI;full][/previewyoutube]
In the [i][b]Tales From the Loop - The Board Game[/b][/i], you take the roles of local kids and play cooperatively to investigate whatever phenomena that threaten the islands (or perhaps just the local video store) and hopefully stop them. Each day starts at school, but as soon as the bell rings you can use whatever time you have before dinner and homework to go exploring! Player actions are integrated, meaning there’s no downtime as you wait for others taking their turn. It also makes cooperating with your fellow players dynamic as you can react to things that happen in a turn and don’t have to plan it all out from the start.

[previewyoutube=AhsBoGTkiTs;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Video Chat Now Available
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/6cc9acc65c7ee984fe90fbf033db05c28f1f53f7.jpg[/img]

Video chat has left beta and is now ready for all players to optionally subscribe to!

In-game video chat is an optional feature that is now available for all users. You can play a game, see each other, and talk all in the same window. If at least one player in your game has a video chat subscription, they can enable video chat for the whole group.

If your account hasn't claimed a 7-day free trial yet, you can test it out for yourself now [i](trial only available via browser - unfortunately limitations with Steam prevent our trial system from working properly)[/i]!

[h2]Activating the video chat subscription[/h2]

Video chat is available only in the game client via web browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Opera, Edge, Safari) or Tabletopia Steam application (Windows, MacOS). When starting up a game room, you will see the following invitation:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/ed17108424b344cc8a6f8620d78e9547b6c75594.png[/img]

If your account has not yet claimed a 7-day free trial, you will be given the option to claim this. Click Apply to start the 7-day free trial period. The 7-day free trial is only available in web browsers, not through Steam (this is due to limitations with the Steam platform and managing free trials).

Otherwise, when you click Apply, you will be given the following prompt to confirm you would like to begin your recurring subscription for video chat:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/8c59a843ae3c62162fa336ccc8fa967a428cd9c2.png[/img]

Click Choose to confirm adding the Video Chat subscription to your account. Video chat is $4.99USD/month. A Premium subscription is not required for the video chat subscription, however please note that they are separate subscriptions.

You can manage your video chat subscription from your [url=https://help.tabletopia.com/knowledge-base/creating-and-managing-profile/#Managing_Profile]profile[/url].

Click Choose to confirm adding the Video Chat subscription to your account. Video chat is $4.99USD/month. A Premium subscription is not required for the video chat subscription, however please note that they are separate subscriptions.

You can manage your video chat subscription from your profile.

[h2]Using video chat[/h2]

When prompted by your browser, you will need to permit Tabletopia to use your webcam and microphone.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/5fc8b408c6a6b6dd1f5d54134d2e750490a15231.jpg[/img]

If you do not have a webcam or do not enable it, you will be able to see and hear others, but they will not see and hear you.

After enabling the video chat, it will load and you will start video conferencing with your friends. There are several options available. You can:

[list]
[*] Show or hide video
[*] Mute/unmute voice
[*] Arrange players in the chat window by row and column
[*] Position this window on the screen by dragging
[*] Choose between available cameras via the ‘settings’ button
[*] Minimize the video chat window (you will still be available to talk to your opponents and hear them)
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/6cc9acc65c7ee984fe90fbf033db05c28f1f53f7.jpg[/img]

You can disconnect from video chat any time by clicking on the red cross. To join it again, click on the video chat icon near the text chat window.

Only a person with a video chat subscription can enable the video chat in a game room. This person doesn’t necessarily need to be the game host; the game can be created by any player. However, if a player with a video chat subscription enables video chat, every other player will get access to the feature for that gaming session.

Two examples of video chat:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/e370e413721afb78c9149d63b7061afa8878a95e.jpg[/img]

[h2]System requirements[/h2]
 
As video chat demands many resources of your system, we strongly recommend using it in the Steam app rather than in a Web browser. Technical constraints of the browsers may cause significant performance slowdown even with two players. We also recommend playing from desktop computers or powerful gaming laptops. Speed of your Internet connection also plays an important role in the smooth performance of Tabletopia with enabled video chat.

You can review this information at any time from our [url=https://help.tabletopia.com/knowledge-base/video-chat/]Knowledge Base article[/url]!

notes.title: Fight for survival... alone!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/015cc4d9407598ff9b44a5cb370a1af6d18c0cbd.jpg[/img]

[i]A mission gone wrong. Tensions continued to mount aboard your colony ship as the days dragged on. An anonymous act of sabotage has sent the ship plummeting to the surface of a frozen uncharted planet. Damaged beyond repair, the scattered remains will do little to protect you from the brutal cold.[/i]

[h3]🚀🚀🚀🚀🚀
1-4 players
60-90 minutes
Engine-building, worker placement, multi-use cards
🚀🚀🚀🚀🚀[/h3]

[previewyoutube=nTQLegpfERE;full][/previewyoutube]
In the engine-building, worker placement game [i][b]Cryo[/b][/i], leaders of separate, hostile factions compete to survive and claim control over the underground caverns on a remote icy planet. You need to act quickly and strategically to avoid further sabotage from other factions. Send drones out from your engineering platform to scavenge resources and save your crew still in cryostasis. Gather different materials to upgrade and customize your platform, fine-tuning new actions to suit your individual strategy. Utilize multi-use cards to your advantage, and claim the underground caverns for your faction to survive.

[previewyoutube=40cvMTKmUT8;full][/previewyoutube]
Though unplanned, a new chapter for humanity has begun. Scavenge, build, explore, and lead your faction to victory within this frozen world before the sun sets!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/f9d1477d2463e171913cc059cc8f0c8e107a1f98.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Trade mysterious artefacts and exhibit the best collection!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/c511b87ecde5b66312691e83d8dbcefbaddb61df.jpg[/img]

A century from now all that remains of Earth is the detritus that humanity left behind. The races of a neighboring solar system have a penchant for artefacts left behind by extinct races. In [i]Excavation Earth[/i], you lead one of these races of alien explorers on their quest to excavate rare human artefacts and curate the ultimate art collection to sell off.

[previewyoutube=KRS1nZWotFA;full][/previewyoutube]
[i]Excavation Earth[/i] is divided into three rounds, each of which starts with players drafting a hand of multi-use cards that will be used to perform actions. Players then take quick turns playing actions that allow them to move their explorers around the world map, excavate for artefacts, and deploy traders to bazaars and influencers to affect prices and wheel and deal on the black market.

[previewyoutube=YlsHw38Or_Y;full][/previewyoutube]
The artefacts you dig up can be either sold to the bazaars housed on one of the aliens' ships that landed on Earth or added to a collection that will be sold off as a coherent art collection to museums back home. Excavation Earth ends after three rounds and the player who makes the most money during the game wins.

[previewyoutube=VJ373FLODL0;full][/previewyoutube]
[i][b]Excavation Earth: It Belongs in a Museum[/b][/i] is the second expansion for [i]Excavation Earth[/i]. It introduces two new alien races, mysterious artefacts, a deck of technology cards and a whole, new museum board. [i]It Belongs in a Museum[/i] adds new ways of scoring that create new paths to playing and winning the game.

notes.title: NEW FUNCTIONALITY: Objects Grouping
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/f0152d04820274582e544e0c34bf62addc953734.jpg[/img]

[url=https://help.tabletopia.com/knowledge-base/objects-grouping/]Objects grouping[/url] functionality lets you select multiple objects of the same type or group and “glue” them together. After being grouped, the objects behave as a single object unless you ungroup them. Grouping functions with the tile, token, card, game piece, counter, & picture counter objects.

[b]To group multiple objects of the same type (tile, token, card, game piece, counter, picture counter):[/b]
[list]
[*] Hold “Shift” and select all the objects you want to group one by one
[*] Right-click any of them > Group
[/list]
[b]To ungroup previously grouped objects:[/b]
[list]
[*] Select the group
[*] Right-click > Ungroup
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/5586f30a770e218cd29001c094ecb9da5ec1fc02.png[/img]

Objects grouping can be used for different purposes. In some games, components must be assembled together at certain moments of gameplay. For example, in [i][b]Argent: the Consortium[/b][/i] players can acquire miniatures of different colors representing their unique abilities. To mark ownership of a miniature, they attach them to bases of their player color. If a miniature and a base are grouped together, they become a single object just like in real life:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/d6ac0f755d424f44b5ed00da283c710377494b0d.jpg[/img]
[i]In Argent: The Consortium, you can use object grouping to attach miniatures to bases[/i]

In [i][b]Dwellings of Eldervale[/b][/i] (coming soon!), buildings are built by attaching a roof to a meeple already placed on the game board. By grouping them together, you will make sure that the building will stay connected until the end of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/566cbfc356fcabf7b73fe30803337e17c13ca77e.jpg[/img]
[i]In Dwellings of Eldervale, object grouping can be used to connect Dwelling Rooftops to Workers[/i]

[h3]Read more about the functionality [url=https://help.tabletopia.com/knowledge-base/objects-grouping/]in our Help[/url]![/h3]

[i]Between Two Castles of Mad King Ludwig[/i] is a competitive tile-drafting game in which each tile is a room in a castle. You work together with the player on your left to design one castle, and with the player on your right on another castle. On each turn you select two tiles from your hand, reveal them, then work with your partners to place them. To win, you have to share your attention and your devotion between two castles.

[i][b]Project L[/b][/i] is a fast-paced, tile-matching brain burner with triple-layer 3D puzzles and lovely acrylic pieces. Challenge your friends to a game of simple design but intricate gameplay that makes a lasting impression!

[previewyoutube=hI0dlmXVqOc;full][/previewyoutube]
The core of the game lies in using your pieces to complete puzzles. Starting with just two basic pieces, you use three actions every turn to develop a powerful engine. With more pieces of various types, you can efficiently complete even the most difficult puzzles. The puzzles you complete award you points or new pieces to further fuel your engine. Can you outsmart your opponents?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/2348cc0178f07c4595ca4c104ec3e2607d82d9f6.jpg[/img]

The [i][b]Finesse[/b][/i] expansion brings extra strategic depth to [i]Project L[/i] through the addition of goals that require each player to fulfill different conditions to get more points during the game. Completing your goals may require making compromises in your strategy or deviating from it altogether, allowing new ways to play [i]Project L[/i].

When you play with [i]Finesse[/i], you have more possible options for scoring points while keeping the same fast-paced gameplay of [i]Project L[/i].

The land of Talon Coast is helpless, as the armies of darkness surge forward, threatening to extinguish the very light of the sun. But there is one last bastion of hope, one final attempt at abating the flood of corruption: Claudius, High Priest of the Temple of Heavenshine, sacrifices the holiest relic of the land to summon the fallen heroes back to life! [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/5504b996992ff60af75b64a285b49c6b96f83db7.jpg[/img]

The isle of Atlantis, your home, is sinking. Will you be able to save your people in time?

[h2][b]4-7 players
60-120 minutes
Cooperative, worker placement, rising tides[/b][/h2]

[i][b]Atlantis Rising[/b][/i] is a co-operative worker placement game in which you must work together with up to five other players to deploy citizens across your homeland, gathering resources in order to build a cosmic gate that can save your people. Workers placed close to the shoreline are more rewarding, but are more likely to be flooded and the actions lost.

[previewyoutube=0us_qA8eNdg;full][/previewyoutube]
Every turn, each player draws a misfortune card that will flood certain locations along the ever-shrinking Atlantis shoreline, or may otherwise work to undermine your efforts to save your people. So you must race to gather the necessary resources to build and power the gate, before the island disappears beneath the waves forever.

[previewyoutube=_TPB1k9nHS4;full][/previewyoutube]
This edition contains all new art and graphic design, created to bring even more attention to the thematic setting of the game. The Athenians Attack phase has been replaced with the Wrath of the Gods phase, requiring more strategic planning and adding to the sense of urgency. Now, instead of placing workers in an Atlantean Navy, players must cooperatively decide to flood a set number of tiles at the end of each round. To further aid them in their task, Councilor player powers have been expanded and made more impactful, and the knowledge deck has similarly been revised and expanded. The variable gate components, once built, no longer offer one-time bonuses, but create new worker placement spots where players can send Atlantean workers to unleash actions to help save their island.

notes.title: Two expansions for the acclaimed AuZtralia game by Martin Wallace!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/c5ec2e93f439f03c11bf4bedc5491c88b0831844.jpg[/img]

[i][b]AuZtralia[/b][/i] is an adventure/exploration game for 1-4 players set in an alternate reality 1930s. The theme is inspired by Martin Wallace's [i]A Study in Emerald[/i]. Following the Restorationist war, the northern hemisphere lands lay poisoned and starvation was the norm. Intrepid adventurers set out to explore and settle new lands. Little did they know, after the war, the surviving Old Ones and their remaining loyal human armies made their way to the outback of Australia to lick their wounds.

[previewyoutube=CxieQhIycC0;full][/previewyoutube]
Build a port, construct railways, mine and farm for food. You’ll need to prepare for the awakening. You’ll need to fight. Everything you do in the game costs time, which is one of AuZtralia's most valued resources.

At a point in time, the Old Ones will wake up and become an active player. They begin to reveal themselves and move, with potentially devastating outcomes.

You’ll need to prepare wisely for the awakening and may have to co-operate with others to defeat the most dangerous Old Ones.

[previewyoutube=uPAiNR8gBt4;full][/previewyoutube]
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The Big Box version of the game along with two brand new expansions are now on Kickstarter. Try the new expansions for yourself now on Tabletopia!

[previewyoutube=J0q0fbCHGr8;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Revenge of the Old Ones[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/85463ac15830c8c9c8e495642a7bcf15eab486fd.jpg[/img]

[i]Revenge of the Old Ones[/i] enables a human player to control the evil forces of the Old Ones. As well as deciding where to place your forces, you can summon terrible creatures from the void to create even more havoc at a time that suits you. Now you can raise Nyarlathotep, summon a Ghoul, or call forth the Hounds of Tindalos to defeat the scourge of humans invading YOUR lands.

To counter the evil mind, the humans have more tools: Outposts, stronger Ports, and extra starting resources.

[h2]TaZmania[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/99775939219f9110b91ddc22d15ab47b24bfe772.jpg[/img]

[i]TaZmania[/i] is a dual-map expansion for [i]AuZtralia[/i] designed specifically for 1-2 players, or 2-3 if playing with the [i]Revenge of the Old Ones[/i] expansion.

The fixed map is surveyed for resources and Old Ones. The second map is randomized through terrain tiles: the central core of the island will remain hidden until you venture near. There's a new terrain type: impassable lakes - and the option of locating your Port anywhere on the coast to get to the heart of the action quickly.

notes.title: More Ways To Play In Hero Realms!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/6b5c3b3f4d68768a131c94d49d391f77b429f8cb.jpg[/img]

Hero Realms is a fantasy-themed deck-building game that is an adaptation of the award-winning Star Realms game - designed by [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgamedesigner/4113/robert-dougherty]Robert Dougherty[/url] & [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgamedesigner/4059/darwin-kastle]Darwin Kastle[/url], and published by [url=https://www.wisewizardgames.com/]Wise Wizard Games[/url]. The game includes basic rules for two-player games.

[previewyoutube=aDdmA_zLeBY;full][/previewyoutube]
Each player starts the game with a ten-card personal deck containing gold (for buying) and weapons (for combat). You start each turn with a new hand of five cards from your personal deck. When your deck runs out of cards, you shuffle your discard pile into your new deck. An 80-card Market deck is shared by all players, with five cards being revealed from that deck to create the Market Row. As you play, you use gold to buy champion cards and action cards from the Market. These champions and actions can generate large amounts of gold, combat, or other powerful effects. You use combat to attack your opponent and their champions. When you reduce your opponent's score (called health) to zero, you win!

[previewyoutube=i-COTj7OYcI;full][/previewyoutube]
Now there are even more ways to play on Tabletopia, with the following improvements added:

[h2]Character Packs[/h2]
Play [i]Hero Realms[/i] as a [i]Cleric, Fighter, Ranger, Thief[/i], or [i]Wizard[/i]! Character Packs add a cool new dimension to player vs player games - giving each player asymmetrical starting decks and unique powers. Each match-up is a unique challenge that will require different strategies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/ca08857cfb887db98ae40eef76d3a5a248d54468.png[/img]

[h2]Ancestry Pack[/h2]
The 20-card Ancestry pack allows you to play Hero Realms as a Dwarf, Elf, Ogre, Orc, or Smallfolk. You may use any race with a generic starting deck, or combine them with any character pack. So you could play as an ogre wizard, an elven ranger, a dwarven fighter, or any one of the 30 new race/class combinations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/ebfd70f6a926f2ff9613939470ab968c6296b25f.png[/img]

[h2]Hidden Areas[/h2]
Our [url=https://tabletopia.com/news/hidden-areas-functionality]recently announced Hidden Areas feature[/url] has now been added to Hero Realms. This will give you a space on the board to place your cards directly from the deck rather than constantly moving cards in and out of your hand. This leads to a much smoother gameplay experience when playing a constantly moving deckbuilder like Hero Realms!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/bbed982e1624f1a7ccd0b4b8c8960b6876e5c61f.png[/img]

[h2]3-4 Player Mode[/h2]
Hero Realms offers multiple options for play at higher player counts, including Free-For-All, Hunter (First Blood), Hunter (Last One Standing), and Hydra. Read more about these multiplayer rules [url=https://www.herorealms.com/multiplayer/]here[/url]!

notes.title: New from Friedemann Friese! Workers try to relax in after-work activities.
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/7bbe7a2ac85940587577a7d9499b3cbfcf1e2341.jpg[/img]

Welcome to [i][b]Feierabend[/b][/i], a.k.a. [i]Finishing Time[/i], the after-worker placement game for 1-6 players by Friedemann Friese!

In [i]Feierabend[/i], you are playing a team of workers (female, male, and non-binary, too). Each day you leave work stressed and look for some fun in the evenings — but thanks to a 70-hour work week and a low income, you don't have many possibilities for relaxation. Sure, you can head to the pub for drinks, go on blind dates to find a partner, or fish or jog outside, but this is not a good work-life balance. It's a rat race.

[previewyoutube=7cjBO5ZTpOA;full][/previewyoutube]
If you really want to relax, you need a higher income for you and your fellow workers — and the women on your team should be paid the same as the men. You want to work fewer hours each week, and taking a vacation would be good, too. Let the union help you fix this depressing lifestyle. This change might stress your employer, of course, but they already earn enough to be able to de-stress their life.

Each turn, place one (or more) of your workers on any available after-work spaces to gain relaxation. Taking leisure time doesn't cost anything, but going to town for amusement requires you to spend hard-earned money. Going on vacation for real relaxation is out of the question until your employer is convinced to grant your workers some time off. When your workers meet partners, you gain access to even better relaxation options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/64787d958fe76a940ad4cd4a32502755cd0dddb6.jpg[/img]

At the pub, workers can relax and have drinks in front of the bar — or they can earn additional income and suffer more stress by working a second job there. You'll want to visit the union office, too, to strike for better working conditions. If you have enough strike tokens, you can force your employer to reduce working hours, increase your income, close the gender gap, or even send you on vacation.

After all your workers have been placed and taken their after-work actions, they are forced to return to work. You place them all on your factory where they then suffer stress, earn income, and gain strike tokens from the union, depending on the current working conditions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/40482985497e575c1049510337db985e4fc79d1d.jpg[/img]

The end of the game is triggered once a team gathers at least 40 relaxation. (In this game, relaxation is considered to be a currency.) Your workers are then placed on after-work spaces and go back to work one more time, after which the most relaxed team wins Feierabend.

Create a better (that is, more relaxing) life for your workers and their partners. Which team will relax the best and win the game? But really every team is a winner since they fought for better working conditions. Workers unite!

[h2][b][url=https://tabletopia.com/games/feierabend]Play it now on Tabletopia![/url][/b][/h2]

[url=https://tabletopia.com/games/feierabend][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/733778004a058936ecc2169b31fb0750a333fb60.jpg[/img][/url]

tags.feature: In Feierabend, you are playing a team of workers (female, male, and non-binary, too).
Each day you leave work stressed and look for some fun in the evenings — but thanks to a 70-hour work week and a low income, you don't have many possibilities for relaxation.
Sure, you can head to the pub for drinks, go on blind dates to find a partner, or fish or jog outside, but this is not a good work-life balance.
It's a rat race.
If you really want to relax, you need a higher income for you and your fellow workers — and the women on your team should be paid the same as the men.
You want to work fewer hours each week, and taking a vacation would be good, too.
Let the union help you fix this depressing lifestyle.
This change might stress your employer, of course, but they already earn enough to be able to de-stress their life.
Each turn, place one (or more) of your workers on any available after-work spaces to gain relaxation.
Taking leisure time doesn't cost anything, but going to town for amusement requires you to spend hard-earned money.
Going on vacation for real relaxation is out of the question until your employer is convinced to grant your workers some time off.
When your workers meet partners, you gain access to even better relaxation options.
At the pub, workers can relax and have drinks in front of the bar — or they can earn additional income and suffer more stress by working a second job there.
You'll want to visit the union office, too, to strike for better working conditions.
If you have enough strike tokens, you can force your employer to reduce working hours, increase your income, close the gender gap, or even send you on vacation.
After all your workers have been placed and taken their after-work actions, they are forced to return to work.
You place them all on your factory where they then suffer stress, earn income, and gain strike tokens from the union, depending on the current working conditions.
The end of the game is triggered once a team gathers at least 40 relaxation.
(In this game, relaxation is considered to be a currency.)
Your workers are then placed on after-work spaces and go back to work one more time, after which the most relaxed team wins Feierabend.
Create a better (that is, more relaxing) life for your workers and their partners.
Which team will relax the best and win the game?
But really every team is a winner since they fought for better working conditions.
Workers unite!

[i][b]Calico[/b][/i] is a puzzly tile-laying game of quilts and cats.

[previewyoutube=QFOGFcZHL74;full][/previewyoutube]
In [i]Calico[/i], players compete to sew the coziest quilt as they collect and place patches of different colors and patterns. Each quilt has a particular pattern that must be followed, and players are also trying to create color and pattern combinations that are not only aesthetically pleasing, but also able to attract the cuddliest cats!

[previewyoutube=PAsUzgeh9GQ;full][/previewyoutube]
Turns are simple. Select a single patch tile from your hand and sew it into your quilt, then draw another patch into your hand from the three available. If you are able to create a color group, you may sew a button onto your quilt. If you are able to create a pattern combination that is attractive to any of the cats, it will come over and curl up on your quilt! At the end of the game, you score points for buttons, cats, and how well you were able to complete your unique quilt pattern.

notes.title: Work together, but DON'T SPEAK! 🤫
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/b7a12c3b35f9448ca5314cbaf6b909ede6cbed3d.jpg[/img]

In [i][b]Silencio[/b][/i], all players form a team together, a team that cannot speak to one another.

You each start with a hand of cards from four suits, and your goal as a team is to discard as many cards as possible — but each card played must have a higher value than the previously played card of the same suit. If a newly played card is the direct successor of the card last played of that color, then you orient the card to show its dark side and suffer the penalty from that card, with the green penalty, for example, forcing the next card played to be green while the blue penalty requires you to give another player one of the face-up cards available from the Oracle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/dd570a7de33a9edeb1e69a46cbc77eb8e7b16df8.jpg[/img]

If a newly played card is not the direct successor of the card last played of that color, then you place the card with the light side face up, taking the bonus depicted on that half of the card if you desire, such as ignoring the next penalty or placing a card from your hand face up in front of you so that anyone could play it.

Five shrines are play — one multicolor shrine and one of each color — and before or after your card play for the turn, you can choose to flip a shrine face down to use the bonus of that color.

If you can't play or have no cards in hand, you must pass, and if all players pass in turn, then the game ends. Your score is based on the number of cards in all players' hands, with 0 being the best score possible. If you find the game difficult, you can include the tavern card that a few times each game allows a player to give limited information about their hand; if the game is too easy, you can remove some or all of the shrines to eliminate those "extra" bonuses.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/afd1a6b2333ffe45674ac8d9a5bf0ea02a415e79.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Hunt, fish, and gather in this Stone Age version of the tile-laying classic.
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/1ad43440a1eb61b1ddbce183f1ea0a1eb9d0ad83.jpg[/img]

[i][b]Carcassonne: Hunters and Gatherers[/b][/i] is a standalone game in the [i][b]Carcassonne [/b][/i]series set in the stone age.

As in other [i][b]Carcassonne [/b][/i]games, players take turns placing tiles to create the landscape and placing meeples to score points from the map they're creating. The player with the most points at the end of the game wins.

[previewyoutube=9dml4XeACyU;full][/previewyoutube]
Instead of cities, roads, and farms, [i][b]Carcassonne: Hunters and Gatherers[/b][/i] has forests, rivers, lakes, and meadows. Players' meeples can represent hunters (when placed in the meadows), gatherers (in a forest), or fishermen (on a river segment). They also have huts, which can be placed on rivers or lakes to get fish from the entire river system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/e42947da1b0483584dffd9eb8ff0931be2fae412.jpg[/img]

It includes many of the familiar mechanics from [i][b]Carcassonne [/b][/i]with a few new rules, including:
- A player who completes a forest with a gold nugget in it gets to immediately draw and place 1 of 12 bonus (menhir) tiles.
- A meadow is worth 2 points for every animal in it, except tigers, which negate certain other animals.
- A river segment is worth the number of tiles in the segment plus the number of fish in the lakes at each end.
- A fishing hut scores at the end of the game and is worth the number of fish in all the lakes connected by rivers.
